> Intended to assist a human reviewer, not replace one — suggestions may be
> incorrect, please verify before acting.


Solid, well-linked docs change. Verified: every internal link/anchor resolves (#reporting-vulnerabilities, #use-tls-termination-maas-33, #manage-api-keys, #release-or-remove-machines, #delete-a-rack-controller, controllers.md/the-machine-life-cycle.md/sso.md/back-up-maas.md/upgrade-maas.md all exist; /reference/cli-reference/config-vault.md is generated at build time by docs/_scripts/generate_cli_docs.py, which lists config-vault; SECURITY.md exists at the repo root); the new page is correctly wired into both the 'Secure MAAS' bullet list (index.md:109) and the hidden toctree (index.md:161) in matching order; sphinxcontrib-mermaid==2.0.2 is a real PyPI release (Apr 2026) whose only deps are sphinx/jinja2/pyyaml (compatible with sphinx==7.4.7) and Python >=3.10 (docs envs use 3.12: .readthedocs.yaml and ubuntu-24.04 CI); the Mermaid diagram itself is syntactically valid (flowchart LR, quoted subgraph titles, cylinder nodes, labelled bidirectional edge all fine). Two deployment-level risks should be addressed before merge: (1) with default config the extension injects mermaid@11.12.1 and d3@7.9.0 from jsdelivr at page-load time, but these docs are also built offline for the snap (MAAS_OFFLINE_DOCS=true make html, snap/snapcraft.yaml:347) where conf.py deliberately gates analytics assets on IS_ONLINE — the snap-served security page will ship unrenderable diagram markup for air-gapped users; (2) .readthedocs.yaml builds formats: [pdf, htmlzip] with sphinx.fail_on_warning: true, and the extension's latex visitor shells out to mmdc (mermaid-cli), which is not in the docs/PDF environment (REQPDFPACKS in docs/Makefile has no Node) — CI only runs make html, so this won't be caught. Minor content nits are in the inline comments.

docs/conf.py.354: sphinxcontrib.mermaid is loaded with all defaults here, so every page containing a diagram gets https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mermaid@11.12.1/dist/mermaid.esm.min.mjs plus https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/d3@7.9.0/dist/d3.min.js injected at view time (install_js in sphinxcontrib/mermaid/__init__.py). These docs are also built offline for the snap (MAAS_OFFLINE_DOCS=true make html, snap/snapcraft.yaml:347) and conf.py already gates the analytics CSS/JS on IS_ONLINE (lines 379-390) — mermaid should follow the same pattern. 2.0.2 resolves mermaid_use_local (and d3_use_local) under html_static_path, so vendoring mermaid.esm.min.mjs into docs/_static/js/ and setting mermaid_use_local here would keep the diagram rendering air-gapped (verify the vendored ESM bundle resolves its imports); otherwise at minimum gate the CDN on IS_ONLINE.

docs/explanation/security.md.15: Rendering caveat beyond syntax (the diagram itself is valid mermaid): with the default mermaid_output_format='raw' this becomes a client-side-rendered <pre class='mermaid'>. For non-HTML builders the extension shells out to mmdc (mermaid-cli) — .readthedocs.yaml builds formats: [pdf, htmlzip] with sphinx.fail_on_warning: true, and neither the RTD env nor REQPDFPACKS (docs/Makefile:17) provides Node/mermaid-cli, so the PDF build either fails on the logged warning or silently drops the diagram. CI only runs make html, so this won't be caught. Consider wrapping the fence in a ```{only} html block (MyST) or installing mermaid-cli for the PDF target.
docs/explanation/security.md.51: Minor consistency nit: the component list adds Temporal (server on the region controller, MAAS Agent on each rack controller connecting to it), but the diagram above omits it — the 'MAAS control plane' subgraph and the rack<->region RPC edge would be its natural home, and its absence leaves the trust-boundary picture incomplete relative to the text. Either add Temporal/Agent nodes or state that the diagram is simplified.

docs/requirements.txt.23: Pin checks out: 2.0.2 is a real PyPI release (Apr 2026), requires Python >=3.10 (docs venvs are 3.12 in .readthedocs.yaml and ubuntu-24.04 CI) and depends only on sphinx/jinja2/pyyaml, so it is compatible with sphinx==7.4.7. Consider bumping to 2.1.1 (current latest): 2.0.3 fixed local JS module imports on root-level pages and deferred rendering of diagrams hidden inside unopened tabs (relevant if a diagram ever lands in a tab-set, as the examples in docs/reuse/mermaid.txt do), and the 2.1.x line adds a global mermaid_config option.

docs/how-to-guides/decommission-maas.md.50: State the expected output: once removal succeeds, 'snap list maas' exits non-zero with 'no matching snaps installed' and 'ls /var/snap/maas/' fails with 'No such file or directory'. Both are the success condition, but as written the step reads as if it should produce output, and a reader may mistake the error for a failed removal.
docs/how-to-guides/decommission-maas.md.59: 'maas config-vault' cannot perform this step: it only provides configure/migrate/status subcommands (src/maasserver/management/commands/config_vault.py:226-263). Deleting the KV secrets and the AppRole is a Vault-side operation (e.g. 'vault kv delete', 'vault auth disable approle'). Link the HashiCorp Vault docs for the deletion step, or drop the CLI-reference link so it doesn't imply config-vault handles cleanup.
